Finding things out

Can someone else check the result?

Keep enough of the method for someone else to check the result.

A closer lookOpen in a larger view ↗

The interactive example has its own motion control. Scroll inside it if you need more room.

A recorded computer experiment

A final number is hard to check on its own. The computer experiment also keeps its starting settings, several measurements and the results of comparison runs.

A separate checking program repeats the calculations from those saved settings. That checks the computer result. It does not replace a test with real equipment.

Words used here
replay
Repeating a calculation from saved settings so its result can be checked.
control
A comparison designed to test whether an apparent effect could have another explanation.
Read the fuller explanation

The four-mode virtual instrument retains more than a returned angle. Its record includes a complex return matrix, populations, loss, control work and the configuration that produced them. A separate verifier replays the saved configuration and checks those records.

The documented design crosses two model settings with four rates and three path controls: forward, reverse and fixed. Those comparisons make a more demanding question possible. Does the proposed effect survive the controls, and what changes when declared imperfections are included?

This room describes that recorded software experiment. It does not run it in your browser, and a successful numerical replay does not supply a physical apparatus. The next threshold remains an actual acquisition with its own calibration and uncertainties.
